Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: an automated test suite. **There are currently zero automated tests in this repo.**

## Why this is worth doing now
A great deal of logic has landed recently, and every bit of it was verified once, by hand, by whoever wrote it — then never again. Several of those verifications caught genuine bugs, which is exactly the evidence that they need to be repeatable. Real examples from the last few days, all of which a test would have caught permanently:

- `creditsFor(0)` returned 1 — a charge for spend that provably did not happen, in the module whose stated purpose is never doing that.
- `\b colou?r \b` did not match "colors" — the word boundary fails on the plural — silently mis-bucketing the most common feedback category.
- `applySeo` double-escaped an already-encoded title, so "Bloom & Co" reached link previews as "Bloom & Co".
- `"CTASection.tsx"` narrated as "the cta section **section**".
- Two separate `v in OBJ` membership guards walked the prototype chain, so `?sort=constructor` produced reachable 500s.
- A nullable FK change rippled into five files.

## Use `node:test` and `node:assert`
Both are Node built-ins. **Do not add a test framework** — no jest, no vitest. `node --test` is the runner.

The obstacle you must solve first: these are `.ts` modules using extensionless imports and the `@/` alias, which bare Node cannot resolve. **`scripts/eval/loader.mjs` already solves exactly this** (a `module.registerHooks` resolver plus a `.env` parser) — read it and reuse it rather than inventing a second mechanism.

## What to cover — pure logic only
Prioritise functions that are pure, load-bearing, and cheap to test. **Do not test anything requiring the database, the network, or a model call.** No Prisma, no HTTP, no `query()`.

Strong candidates (read each before deciding):
- `lib/credits.ts` — `costMicros`, `creditsFor`, `estimateCredits`, and the new repair-pass settlement logic. The zero case and the rounding floor both matter.
- `lib/build-narration.ts` — `narrateTool`, `describePath`. Plurals, initialisms (FAQ, CTA), absolute vs project-relative paths.
- `lib/feedback-intent.ts` — `classifyFollowUp`. Include the regression cases: "great, now make the colors warmer" must be `visual`, not `praise`.
- `lib/site-seo.ts` — `applySeo`, `robotsTxt`, `sitemapXml`, and the entity round-trip.
- `app/api/projects/[id]/seo/head.ts` — `applyHead`. Idempotency and single-quoted attributes.
- `lib/moderation.ts` — the rules. **The false-positive cases matter more than the true positives**: a real product login page, a coffee shop using formsubmit.co, and a "never share your seed phrase" explainer must all pass clean.
- `lib/assets/index.ts` — `findAssets`. Include "french flag" returning France, which was a real bug.
- `lib/flags.ts` — `rolloutBucket` stability and cross-flag decorrelation, if they can be reached without a DB.
- `lib/zip.ts` — CRC and the STORE-vs-deflate fallback.

**Every one of the bugs listed at the top must have a test that fails against the old behaviour.** That is the acceptance criterion for this task, not raw coverage.

## Also
- A `scripts/test/README.md` explaining how to run it and the rule about what does not belong here.
- Report the exact command. If adding a `package.json` script would help, **describe it — do not edit package.json**, it is on the forbidden list.

## Constraints
- YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT FILES UNDER `tests/` and `scripts/test/`.
- DO NOT modify any application code. **If a test fails because the code is wrong, do NOT fix the code** — report it. That is a finding, and it is the most valuable thing you can produce.
- DO NOT modify: package.json, prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/ or app/, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env.
- No new npm dependencies.
- Tests must be deterministic and fast. No wall-clock sleeps, no random input without a fixed seed.
- Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH stay clean — currently ZERO errors and ZERO warnings.** Note other agents are editing `lib/credits.ts`, `app/api/generate/route.ts`, `app/projects/[id]/**`, `app/api/site/**` and `lib/site-forms.ts` right now; transient errors in those are not yours.

## Report back
The exact run command, how many tests and what they cover, **every genuine bug the suite found** (with file and line), and which candidate modules you could not test without a database and why.

1	// Classifies a follow-up request into a coarse intent bucket.
2	//
3	// The point: what someone types AFTER a build is the sharpest quality signal
4	// the product produces, and it is currently thrown away. If "the copy is
5	// generic" is 40% of follow-ups and "it's broken" is 2%, that ranks the next
6	// prompt change for us. Nothing else we collect answers that question.
7	//
8	// Deliberately heuristic, and deliberately NOT a model call:
9	//  - It runs on the request path of every edit. A model call there would add
10	//    latency and cost to every single build to produce a dashboard number.
11	//  - The cost of a wrong answer is one miscounted row in an aggregate. That is
12	//    a completely different risk profile from, say, content moderation, where
13	//    a keyword heuristic would be indefensible because a wrong answer blocks a
14	//    real customer's site.
15	//
16	// Treat the output as a weak signal in aggregate, never as a fact about an
17	// individual request. If the buckets ever start driving something with real
18	// consequences, replace this with a proper classifier first.
19	
20	export const INTENTS = [
21	  "broken", // it doesn't work / it's blank / error
22	  "visual", // colours, fonts, spacing, "ugly"
23	  "content", // wording, copy, text, names, prices
24	  "layout", // move/reorder/resize/structure
25	  "add", // add a section, page, feature
26	  "remove", // delete something
27	  "praise", // no change requested
28	  "other",
29	] as const;
30	
31	export type Intent = (typeof INTENTS)[number];
32	
33	// Ordered: the FIRST match wins, so the list runs most-specific first.
34	// "broken" outranks everything — a blank page is not a styling note even when
35	// the user politely phrases it as one.
36	//
37	// Note the plural-tolerant endings (`colou?rs?`, `fonts?`). `\bcolou?r\b`
38	// does NOT match "colors": the trailing \b fails against the s. That silently
39	// mis-bucketed the single most common visual request until a test caught it.
40	const RULES: { intent: Intent; pattern: RegExp }[] = [
41	  {
42	    intent: "broken",
43	    pattern:
44	      /\b(broken|not working|doesn'?t work|blank|white screen|empty page|errors?|crash(ed|ing|es)?|bugs?|nothing (shows|happens|loads)|won'?t load|failed)\b/i,
45	  },
46	  {
47	    intent: "remove",
48	    pattern: /\b(remove|delete|get rid of|take out|drop the|don'?t (want|need))\b/i,
49	  },
50	  {
51	    intent: "add",
52	    pattern:
53	      /\b(add|include|insert|another|a new|also (want|need)|can (you|we) (add|put)|put in|create a)\b/i,
54	  },
55	  {
56	    intent: "visual",
57	    pattern:
58	      /\b(colou?rs?|fonts?|typefaces?|bolder|darker|lighter|backgrounds?|gradients?|styl(e|es|ing)|themes?|ugly|bland|generic|boring|prettier|nicer|modern|rounded|shadows?|spacing|padding|margins?|warmer|cooler|brighter|vibrant)\b/i,
59	  },
60	  {
61	    intent: "layout",
62	    pattern:
63	      /\b(move|reorder|swap|above|below|left|right|centre|center|align|bigger|smaller|wider|narrower|full width|layouts?|position|order|top|bottom|grids?|columns?|stack)\b/i,
64	  },
65	  {
66	    intent: "content",
67	    pattern:
68	      /\b(text|copy|wording|words?|headlines?|titles?|headings?|paragraphs?|change .* to|rename|spelling|typos?|prices?|pricing|phone|address|emails?|hours|name)\b/i,
69	  },
70	];
71	
72	// Checked only AFTER every actionable rule misses. "Great, now make the
73	// colours warmer" is a change request that opens politely, not praise — so
74	// praise must never outrank a bucket that names actual work. Matching a
75	// keyword anywhere (rather than requiring the whole string to be praise) is
76	// what lets "wow this is amazing" through.
77	const PRAISE =
78	  /\b(wow|nice|great|perfect|awesome|amazing|love it|looks good|looks great|thanks?|thank you|beautiful|excellent|brilliant|exactly)\b/i;
79	
80	/**
81	 * Best-guess bucket for a follow-up request. Returns "other" when nothing
82	 * matches, which is a real answer — an "other" rate that climbs means the
83	 * rules have drifted from how people actually talk.
84	 */
85	export function classifyFollowUp(prompt: string): Intent {
86	  const text = prompt.trim();
87	  if (!text) return "other";
88	
89	  for (const rule of RULES) {
90	    if (rule.pattern.test(text)) return rule.intent;
91	  }
92	  if (PRAISE.test(text)) return "praise";
93	  return "other";
94	}

1	/**
2	 * The asset library's front door: one catalogue and one query function over
3	 * every inlinable asset Kodely can hand a generated site.
4	 *
5	 * THE SEAM
6	 * {@link findAssets} is deliberately shaped like a tool call. A future agent
7	 * tool ("search_assets") should be able to forward its arguments straight
8	 * through and hand the model back `AssetMatch[]` — each match already carries
9	 * a paste-ready `source` and a one-line `usage`, so the model never has to
10	 * invent SVG geometry or guess at a CSS incantation. Wiring that tool into
11	 * lib/agent.ts is not this module's job; being callable from it is.
12	 *
13	 * WHY EVERY MATCH IS INLINABLE
14	 * Generated sites run under `default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:;
15	 * connect-src 'none'` with no way to add npm packages, so a hosted asset —
16	 * however convenient — would fail silently at serve time. Every `source`
17	 * string here is either markup, CSS, or a `data:` URI, all of which survive
18	 * that sandbox. See the header comments in ./icons.ts and ./patterns.ts.
19	 */
20	
21	import {
22	  ICONS,
23	  iconCategories,
24	  iconDataUri,
25	  iconJsx,
26	  iconSvg,
27	  toJsx,
28	  type Icon,
29	  type IconWeight,
30	} from "./icons";
31	import { FLAGS, flagSvg, type Flag } from "./flags";
32	import {
33	  DIVIDERS,
34	  GRADIENTS,
35	  MESHES,
36	  PATTERNS,
37	  TEXTURES,
38	  avatarColors,
39	  dividerSvg,
40	  initialsAvatarSvg,

44	export type AssetKind = "icon" | "flag" | "gradient" | "mesh" | "texture" | "divider" | "pattern" | "avatar";
45	
46	export const ASSET_KINDS: AssetKind[] = [
47	  "icon",
48	  "flag",
49	  "gradient",
50	  "mesh",
51	  "texture",
52	  "divider",
53	  "pattern",
54	  "avatar",
55	];
56	
57	export type AssetMatch = {
58	  /** Stable, namespaced: "icon:phone", "flag:fr", "gradient:sunset". */
59	  id: string;
60	  kind: AssetKind;
61	  name: string;
62	  keywords: string[];
63	  format: "jsx" | "svg" | "css" | "text";
64	  /** The thing to paste into the generated site. */
65	  source: string;
66	  /** One line telling the caller where this goes. */
67	  usage: string;
68	  /** Alternative representations — raw svg, data URI, Tailwind class, colours. */
69	  variants?: Record<string, string>;
70	  /** Relevance for the query that produced this. 0 when listed rather than searched. */
71	  score: number;
72	};
73	
74	export type FindAssetsOptions = {
75	  /** Restrict to one or more kinds. Omit for everything. */
76	  kind?: AssetKind | AssetKind[];
77	  /** Default 20, capped at 100. */
78	  limit?: number;
79	  /** Icon stroke weight for the emitted `source`. Default "regular". */
80	  weight?: IconWeight;
81	};

90	  id: string;
91	  kind: AssetKind;
92	  name: string;
93	  /** Lowercased, de-duplicated search terms. */

95	  render: (opts: FindAssetsOptions) => Rendered;

98	function iconEntry(icon: Icon): Entry {

100	    id: `icon:${icon.id}`,
101	    kind: "icon",
102	    name: icon.name,
103	    keywords: icon.keywords,
104	    render: (opts) => ({
105	      format: "jsx",
106	      source: iconJsx(icon.id, { weight: opts.weight ?? "regular", size: null, className: "h-6 w-6" }) ?? "",
107	      usage:

109	      variants: {
110	        svg: iconSvg(icon.id, { weight: opts.weight ?? "regular" }) ?? "",

122	// name, so "French Guiana" owns the literal token "french" and scored a full
123	// keyword hit, while France could only be reached through a synonym — which is
124	// deliberately discounted, and is only consulted when the literal token scores
125	// zero. "french flag" therefore returned French Guiana, French Polynesia and
126	// French Southern Territories, and not France. Same for "british" (British
127	// Indian Ocean Territory) and "american" (American Samoa).

8	// deploy. `deploy.sh` on this project has a history of shipping stale code,
9	// and a kill switch that needs a deploy is not a kill switch — it is a
10	// postmortem action item. Flipping a row here takes effect everywhere within
11	// one cache TTL (see FLAG_CACHE_TTL_MS below), with no build, no restart and
12	// no risk of shipping whatever else happened to be sitting on main.

15	// lib/events.ts useful:
16	//
17	// 1. KEYS ARE A CLOSED SET. FLAGS below is the whole vocabulary. Free-text
18	//    flag keys rot exactly like free-text event names: someone checks
19	//    "publish_enabled" while the admin page writes "publishing.enabled", the
20	//    check silently reads a missing row forever, and the kill switch that
21	//    everyone believes exists does nothing on the day it matters.

24	//    "the thing is broken/off" — inverted flags are how someone turns
25	//    generation OFF at 3am while trying to turn it off.

# The test suite

Pure-logic tests for the modules where a wrong answer is expensive: what we
charge, what we publish, what we refuse to publish, and what we tell the user
is happening.

## Running it

From the repo root:

```
node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test "tests/*.test.mjs"
```

Keep the quotes. Node expands the glob itself; letting a shell do it breaks on
Windows, and passing the bare directory (`--test tests/`) fails because the
resolver hook in `scripts/eval/loader.mjs` intercepts the directory specifier.

Everything is in-process and pure, so the whole suite runs in about a second.

**As of the last run: 209 tests, 198 pass, 11 fail.** The 11 failures are all in
`tests/open-bugs.test.mjs` and are all real bugs in application code — see
[Known failures](#known-failures) below. To run only the part that should be
green, and get a zero exit code:

```
node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test --test-skip-pattern="^BUG:" "tests/*.test.mjs"
```

One file, one module:

```
node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test tests/credits.test.mjs
```

One test by name:

```
node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test --test-name-pattern="creditsFor" "tests/*.test.mjs"
```

### A package.json script

`package.json` was out of scope for the change that added this suite, so there
is no `npm test` yet. Adding one is two lines:

```json
"test": "node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test \"tests/*.test.mjs\"",
"test:green": "node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test --test-skip-pattern=\"^BUG:\" \"tests/*.test.mjs\""
```

## How .ts modules load under bare Node

`node --test` runs plain Node. Node 24 strips TypeScript types natively, but
its ESM resolver still demands full specifiers, and the app uses extensionless
imports (`./models`) and the `@/` tsconfig alias throughout.

That problem was already solved for the eval harness, so
`scripts/test/register.mjs` **reuses `scripts/eval/loader.mjs`** —
`registerTsResolution()` and `quietNodeWarnings()` — rather than registering a
second, subtly different resolver. Two mechanisms for one problem is how "it
passes under the tests but not under the evals" starts.

The one thing it does *not* reuse is `loadEnv()`. That function throws unless
`KODELY_FOUNDATION_DIR` points at an installed foundation checkout, because the
eval harness runs real builds. This suite must stay runnable on a laptop with
no `.env`, no foundation and no database, so `register.mjs` sets the two
module-scope environment variables the code under test actually reads
(`KODELY_SITES_BASE`, `NODE_ENV`) and nothing else.

No test framework, and no new dependency: `node:test` and `node:assert` only.

## What does NOT belong here

**Nothing that touches the database, the network, or a model call.** No Prisma
queries, no `fetch`, no `runAgent`, no `buildSite`. If a test needs a row to
exist, it is in the wrong file.

That is a hard line, not a preference:

- These tests run on every developer's machine, including one with a `.env`
  pointing at production. A suite that can write is a suite that can write
  there.
- A test that needs a database is a test nobody runs, and a test nobody runs is
  worse than no test — it is a green badge over an unverified module.
- Determinism. No wall-clock sleeps, no `Date.now()`-dependent assertions, no
  unseeded random input. Every fixture here is a literal; where a test needs
  many inputs (bucket distribution, CRC round trips) it generates them from a
  fixed sequence, never from `Math.random()`.

Some modules import `./db` transitively — `lib/credits.ts` and `lib/flags.ts`
both do — and that is fine: constructing a `PrismaClient` opens no connection.
It is *queries* that are banned, so those modules are tested only through their
pure exports.

For anything that genuinely needs the real pipeline, use the eval harness
(`scripts/eval`) instead. It exists for exactly that and is deliberately kept
separate.

### Modules deliberately left untested

| Module | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/credits.ts` — `getBalance`, `grantCredits`, `chargeForBuild`, `averageBuildCredits`, `spentInWindow`, `getSpendCapStatus` | Every one is a `db.creditLedger` / `db.user` / `db.build` query. The arithmetic they *wrap* (`costMicros`, `creditsFor`, `settleBuild`) is covered. |
| `lib/flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `listFlags`, `setFlag`, `seedFlags`, `deleteOrphanFlag`, the cache | All read or write the `FeatureFlag` table. `rolloutBucket`, `clampRolloutPct` and the declared spec table are covered; the resolution order in `isEnabled` needs a fake Prisma client and belongs in an integration suite. |
| `lib/moderation.ts` — `recordModerationFindings` | Writes `ModerationFinding` rows. The analyzer it records the output of is covered in full. |
| `app/admin/users/page.tsx`, `app/admin/content/page.tsx` — `isSortKey` | Not exported, and the module is a Next server component that pulls in `next/navigation` and Prisma at import time. The identical bug in the two *exported* twins (`lib/flags.ts` `isFlagKey`, `app/admin/health/data.ts` `isWindowKey`) is covered instead. |
| `lib/agent.ts`, `lib/agent-sdk.ts`, `lib/build-site.ts`, `lib/enhance.ts` | Model calls and real builds. That is what `scripts/eval` is for. |

## Layout

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/credits.test.mjs` | `costMicros`, `creditsFor`, `sumUsage`, `settleBuild`, `estimateCredits` |
| `tests/build-narration.test.mjs` | `describePath`, `narrateTool` |
| `tests/feedback-intent.test.mjs` | `classifyFollowUp` |
| `tests/site-seo.test.mjs` | `siteBaseUrl`, `applySeo`, `robotsTxt`, `sitemapXml` |
| `tests/seo-head.test.mjs` | `applyHead`, `escapeAttr` |
| `tests/moderation.test.mjs` | the heuristic rules, `blockingFindings`, the provider seam |
| `tests/assets.test.mjs` | `findAssets`, `getAsset`, `listAssets`, `assetCatalogSummary` |
| `tests/flags.test.mjs` | `rolloutBucket`, `clampRolloutPct`, the flag/spec vocabulary |
| `tests/zip.test.mjs` | `zipStream` — CRC, STORE-vs-deflate, zip-slip, DOS dates, structure |
| `tests/open-bugs.test.mjs` | **fails on purpose** — see below |

Every test in the first nine files pins behaviour that is correct today,
including a regression case for each of the bugs found by hand over the last
few days: `creditsFor(0)`, the `colou?r` plural, the `applySeo` entity round
trip, `"CTASection.tsx"`, and `"french flag"`.

## Known failures

`tests/open-bugs.test.mjs` asserts the behaviour the code claims — in its own
comments — and every test in it fails today. They are not `skip`ped and not
marked `todo`, because a suite that quietly tolerates a known-wrong answer is
how the answer stays wrong. Each test names the file and line, and each goes
green the moment the bug is fixed, with no rewriting.

1. **`lib/site-seo.ts:155-160` — `og:title` still double-escapes.** The entity
   round trip was fixed for `description` (line 142 decodes first) but the
   `og:title` upsert passes the already-encoded title straight to `escapeHtml`,
   so "Bloom & Co" reaches link previews as `Bloom & Co`. Same bug, same
   module, on the tag link previews read first.
2. **`$`-substitution in `String.prototype.replace` replacements** —
   `lib/site-seo.ts:114,117,135` and `app/api/projects/[id]/seo/head.ts:23,40,41`.
   The replacement is built as a string, so `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'` and `$1` are
   interpreted as substitution patterns. `escapeHtml`/`escapeAttr` do not
   escape `$`, and `$` is ordinary in a business name ("Everything $1 Store").
   `` $` `` splices the entire preceding document into a meta attribute, and
   `applySeo` runs on every read of every published site. Fix: pass a replacer
   function.
3. **Prototype-chain membership guards** — `lib/flags.ts:167` (`isFlagKey`) and
   `app/admin/health/data.ts:22` (`isWindowKey`), plus the unexported twins at
   `app/admin/users/page.tsx:37` and `app/admin/content/page.tsx:53`.
   `app/admin/sites` was fixed by switching to `hasKey`
   (`app/admin/sites/ui.tsx:25`); four guards of the same shape were left
   behind. `?sort=constructor` and `?window=constructor` are reachable 500s,
   and in `lib/flags.ts` the guard is the only thing stopping `setFlag` from
   writing a junk key. Fix: `Object.hasOwn`, or reuse `hasKey`.
4. **`lib/assets/index.ts:126,543` — `"american flag"` returns American Samoa.**
   The `DEMONYMS` comment claims the fix covers "american"; it does not.
   France and the UK only win because the score tie is broken by
   `id.localeCompare` and the alphabet happens to run the right way
   (`flag:fr` < `flag:gf`, `flag:gb` < `flag:io`). For the US it runs the wrong
   way (`flag:as` < `flag:us`).
5. **`lib/assets/index.ts:505-512` — `findAssets("coffee shop")` returns `[]`.**
   That is the docstring's own example. `shop` expands to
   store/shopping/cart/bag, the coffee icon carries none of them, so every
   entry misses a token.

## What landed

**209 tests, 198 pass, 11 fail, ~0.9 s.** All 11 failures are in `tests/open-bugs.test.mjs` and are genuine application bugs (below). Files created, all under the allowed paths:

- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\scripts\test\register.mjs` — reuses `registerTsResolution()` + `quietNodeWarnings()` from `scripts/eval/loader.mjs`. Deliberately does **not** call `loadEnv()` (it throws without `KODELY_FOUNDATION_DIR`); instead sets `KODELY_SITES_BASE` and `NODE_ENV` before first import, since both are read at module scope.
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\scripts\test\README.md`
- `tests/credits.test.mjs` (27) · `build-narration.test.mjs` (22) · `feedback-intent.test.mjs` (17) · `site-seo.test.mjs` (26) · `seo-head.test.mjs` (14) · `moderation.test.mjs` (28) · `assets.test.mjs` (25) · `flags.test.mjs` (18) · `zip.test.mjs` (21) · `open-bugs.test.mjs` (11)

All six bugs from the brief have a test that fails against the old behaviour: `creditsFor(0) === 0`, `"make the colors warmer" → visual`, the `applySeo` description entity round-trip, `"CTASection.tsx" → "the CTA section"`, `"french flag" → flag:fr`, and the prototype-chain guards (the last as red tests, see #3).

Both gates are clean: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` produce zero output. `.mjs` tests sit outside `tsconfig.include` by design.

## Genuine bugs the suite found

1. **`lib/site-seo.ts:155-160` — `og:title` still double-escapes.** The decode-then-escape fix landed on `description` (line 142) but not on `og:title`, which passes the already-encoded title straight to `escapeHtml`. `<title>Bloom & Co</title>` → `og:title content="Bloom &amp; Co"`. Same bug, same module, on the tag link previews read first.

2. **`$`-substitution in replacement strings** — `lib/site-seo.ts:114,117,135` and `app/api/projects/[id]/seo/head.ts:23,40,41`. Replacements are built as strings, so `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'`, `$1` are treated as substitution patterns; `escapeHtml`/`escapeAttr` don't escape `$`. Project name `Everything $1 Store` loses the `$1`; `` $` `` splices the **entire preceding document** into a meta attribute. `applySeo` runs on every read of every published site. Fix is a replacer function.

3. **Four `v in OBJ` guards still walk the prototype chain.** `app/admin/sites` was fixed with `hasKey` (`app/admin/sites/ui.tsx:25`), but these were missed: `lib/flags.ts:167` (`isFlagKey`), `app/admin/health/data.ts:22` (`isWindowKey`), `app/admin/users/page.tsx:37` and `app/admin/content/page.tsx:53` (`isSortKey`). `?sort=constructor` and `?window=constructor` are still reachable 500s. In `lib/flags.ts` it's worse than a 500 — that guard is the only thing stopping `setFlag` (a Server Action, i.e. a public endpoint) writing a junk key, and `FLAG_SPECS.constructor` is a function so `spec.whenUnset` is `undefined`.

4. **`lib/assets/index.ts:126,543` — `"american flag"` returns American Samoa.** The `DEMONYMS` comment claims the fix covers "american"; it doesn't. France and the UK only win because the score tie is broken by `id.localeCompare` and the alphabet runs the right way (`flag:fr` < `flag:gf`, `flag:gb` < `flag:io`). For the US it runs the wrong way (`flag:as` < `flag:us`). The shipped fix is load-bearing on luck.

5. **`lib/assets/index.ts:505-512` — `findAssets("coffee shop")` returns `[]`.** That is the docstring's own example. `shop` expands to store/shopping/cart/bag; the coffee icon carries none, so the AND drops every entry.

6. **`lib/feedback-intent.ts:56-69` — `"the copy is generic"` buckets as `visual`.** That exact phrase is the module header's headline example of a *content* complaint. `generic` sits in the visual pattern and visual is tested before content, so "copy" never gets a look in. Same class as the `colou?r` plural bug: an over-broad token in a higher-priority rule.

Minor, reported without a red test: `siteBaseUrl` compares the Host header case-sensitively, so `ABC.KODELY.SITE` falls through to the path form and emits a wrong canonical/og:url. Also, `findAssets("electrician")` returns `icon:wrench` above `icon:zap` — the same alphabetical tie-break as #4, but both icons are defensible, so the test accepts either.

## Not tested, and why

- `lib/credits.ts` — `getBalance`, `grantCredits`, `chargeForBuild`, `averageBuildCredits`, `spentInWindow`, `getSpendCapStatus`: all Prisma queries. The arithmetic they wrap is fully covered.
- `lib/flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `listFlags`, `setFlag`, `seedFlags`, `deleteOrphanFlag`, and the TTL cache: all read/write `FeatureFlag`. `isEnabled`'s resolution order needs a fake Prisma client and belongs in an integration suite. `rolloutBucket`, `clampRolloutPct` and the spec table are covered.
- `lib/moderation.ts` — `recordModerationFindings`: writes rows. The analyzer it records is covered in full.
- `app/admin/users/page.tsx` and `app/admin/content/page.tsx` — `isSortKey` is not exported and the module pulls `next/navigation` + Prisma at import. Covered via the two exported twins with the identical bug.
- `lib/agent.ts`, `lib/agent-sdk.ts`, `lib/build-site.ts`, `lib/enhance.ts` — model calls and real builds; that's `scripts/eval`.

Note that `lib/credits.ts` and `lib/flags.ts` *are* imported (they pull in `./db` transitively) — constructing a `PrismaClient` opens no connection, and no test issues a query.
